_readme: Spoken numbers in Relay's tier-1 languages, so a preacher can say the chapter
and verse in their own language: 'Yohana sura ya tatu, mstari wa kumi na sita'.
DATA, NOT RUST — same reason as book_aliases.json. A wrong numeral does not
fail safely: it silently shows a DIFFERENT VERSE. If 'tisa' were mapped to 8
instead of 9, nobody would notice until a service. A native speaker can correct
a number here in a one-line pull request without touching Rust.
THE GRAMMAR IS IN THE CODE; ONLY THE WORDS ARE HERE. The shape of these two
languages happens to be the same, which is why one state machine handles both:
tens + connector + ones     ishirini na tatu = 23   ashirin da uku = 23
ten  + connector + ones     kumi na tatu     = 13   goma sha uku   = 13
THE ONE THING THAT IS NOT LIKE ENGLISH, and it matters:
The hundred MULTIPLIER COMES AFTER the hundred word.
mia moja  = 100   (literally 'hundred one')   NOT 101
mia mbili = 200                               NOT 102
ɗari biyu = 200                               NOT 102
English puts it before ('two hundred'), so the English parser would have read
'mia mbili' as 100 + 2 = 102 and shown Psalm 102 when the preacher said 200.
`hundred_post` marks the words that behave this way.
A connector disambiguates: 'mia moja' (no connector) is 1×100, while
'mia na tatu' (connector) is 100+3. Both are handled.
Sources: Swahili — Omniglot / Languages and Numbers. Hausa — Omniglot /
Languages and Numbers / teachyourselfhausa.com.

sw._ones_note: kwanza/pili are the ORDINALS (first/second). 'mstari wa kwanza' = verse one — how a preacher actually says it. From 3 up, the ordinal and cardinal are the same word.
sw._linkers_note: Grammatical glue: 'sura YA tatu', 'mstari WA kwanza'. Skipped between a keyword and its number — never treated as numbers themselves.

ha._ones_note: farko/fari = 'first'. 'aya ta farko' = verse one. Hooked ɗ and ƙ fold to d and k automatically, so both spellings are safe to list.
ha._connectors_note: 'sha' builds the teens (goma sha uku = 13); 'da' joins tens and units (ashirin da uku = 23).
